messages.content:
You are writing for a bank's internal auditor, in UK English.
For each finding, write 2-3 plain sentences: what is wrong, why it matters, what to do.
Use ONLY the numbers given. Do not add, round, combine or calculate numbers.
Do not name customers. Return JSON: {"findings": {"<id>": "<text>", ...}}

{"CV1": "Money order deposits (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions. No rule can fire on money order deposits (in), so £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for money order deposits (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "BL1": "50 customers with no case look highly unusual. top 50 of 47,056 unflagged customers. These customers never reached the alarm level, but their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Top reasons: 6334452196: money in (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 22 (top 0.5% of customers) | 1896192273: money in from abroad (£) 333,931 (top 0.7% of customers); most payments in 30 days 247 (top 1% of customers); money in (£) 333,931 (top 1% of customers) | 8961996693: money in (£) 447,072 (top 0.3% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 406,901 (top 0.4% of customers); most deposits in one day 2 (top 2% of customers) Suggested fix: Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.", "BL3": "The valued-client list hides highly unusual customers. 5 of 5 suppressed customers in the top 2% most unusual. These customers scored enough for a case but were exempted as valued clients, and their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Suggested fix: Remove automatic suppression; review valued clients like anyone else.", "CA2": "Strong red flag worth only 1 point: R02_cash_near_limit. 1 pts, right 26.9% of the time (19-37%, n=93). 3+ cash deposits between £9,000 and £9,999 within 30 days. When investigators reviewed customers this rule flagged, 27% were laundering, 3.8x the average, yet it adds only 1 of the 20 points needed for a case. Suggested fix: Raise R02_cash_near_limit from 1 to about 5 points.", "AD1": "Advisory pattern not caught: Business credit‑card repayments to many individuals. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £2,115,842. The advisory warns: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\". 25 customers match this pattern, but only a transaction-count rule can see them, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: Assume at least ten distinct cardholders over a 90‑day window; each repayment between £250‑£2,500 Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: business credit‑card repayments to many individuals (red flag: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\").", "AD2": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple small money orders paid in same day. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £668,454. The advisory warns: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\". 25 customers match this pattern, but no rule can see these transactions, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: Assume at least two money orders per day, combined total <£2,500, repeated on at least two separate days Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple small money orders paid in same day (red flag: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\").", "CV2": "Credit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,095,313,643. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card payments (out).", "CV3": "Debit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,085,585,977. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for debit card payments (out).", "CV4": "Credit card repayments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £63,913,161. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card repayments (out).", "CA1": "Weak rule over-weighted: R01_large_cash. 10 pts, right 2.0% of the time (1-4%, n=541). Cash deposit at or over £10,000. Only 2% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 10 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 points to cut false alarms.", "CA3": "Weak rule over-weighted: R04_large_wire. 5 pts, right 3.7% of the time (3-5%, n=1023). Wire or cross-border payment of £50,000 or more. Only 4% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 5 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 points to cut false alarms."}

reply: {"findings":{"CV1":"Money order deposits (in) are not monitored – 0 % of £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions were checked, leaving £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers unchecked. This gap means potentially illicit funds are never screened, increasing AML risk. Add scenario rules for money order deposits (in) covering amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","BL1":"Fifty unflagged customers appear among the most unusual of the bank’s 47,056 unflagged accounts. Their activity includes money‑in of £831,312 (top 0.1 % of customers) and £333,931 (top 0.7 %), money‑in from abroad of £831,312 and £333,931, high‑risk‑country transactions (22) and high deposit counts, indicating elevated risk. Send these customers for manual review, starting with the highest‑ranked case.","BL3":"The valued‑client list hides highly unusual customers. All 5 of the 5 suppressed customers are in the top 2 % most unusual and would otherwise generate a case. Remove automatic suppression and review valued clients like any other customer.","CA2":"The red‑flag R02_cash_near_limit only contributes 1 point despite flagging cash deposits between £9,000 and £9,999 that occur 3 + times in 30 days. It is correct 26.9 % of the time (19‑37 %, n = 93) and when it does fire 27 % of those customers are laundering – 3.8 × the average – yet it provides only 1 of the 20 points needed for a case. Raise R02_cash_near_limit from 1 to about 5 points.","AD1":"The advisory for business credit‑card repayments to many individuals matches 25 customers, yet only one case has been generated because only a transaction‑count rule sees them. This pattern involves repayments of £250‑£2,500 to at least ten distinct cardholders over a 90‑day window and represents £2,115,842 of exposure. Add a scenario for business credit‑card repayments to many individuals as described in the advisory.","AD2":"The advisory for multiple small money orders on the same day matches 25 customers, but no rule currently detects the pattern, resulting in only one case. The pattern is defined as at least two money orders per day with a combined value just below £2,500, repeated on at least two separate days, involving £668,454. Add a scenario for multiple small money orders paid in the same day as per the advisory.","CV2":"Credit‑card payments (out) are only screened by the R06_velocity rule, which counts payments for a total volume of £3,095,313,643 but never evaluates amount, country or counter‑party. This lack of detail leaves large or suspicious outflows unchecked. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for credit‑card payments (out).","CV3":"Debit‑card payments (out) are only screened by the R06_velocity rule, which counts payments for a total volume of £3,085,585,977 but never evaluates amount, country or counter‑party. This lack of detail leaves large or suspicious outflows unchecked. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for debit‑card payments (out).","CV4":"Credit‑card repayments (out) are only screened by the R06_velocity rule, which counts payments for a total volume of £63,913,161 but never evaluates amount, country or counter‑party. This lack of detail leaves large or suspicious outflows unchecked. Add amount‑based and counter‑party rules for credit‑card repayments (out).","CA1":"Rule R01_large_cash carries 10 points but is correct only 2.0 % of the time (1‑4 %, n = 541); cash deposits at or over £10,000 therefore generate many false alarms. Reducing its weight to about 1 point will cut unnecessary alerts. Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 point.","CA3":"Rule R04_large_wire carries 5 points but is correct only 3.7 % of the time (3‑5 %, n = 1023); wire or cross‑border payments of £50,000 or more therefore generate many false alarms. Reducing its weight to about 1 point will cut unnecessary alerts. Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 point."}}
